### What issue are you seeing?
Plugins installed from the remote curated marketplace load in interactive sessions but never in `codex exec`. `codex plugin list` reports:

    superpowers@openai-curated-remote   installed, enabled  6.4.2

Skill roots in the developer message of an interactive session (originator `codex-tui`):

    r0 .codex/skills   r1 .agents/skills   r2 .codex/skills/.system
    r3 .codex/plugins/cache/openai-bundled
    r4 .codex/plugins/cache/openai-curated-remote
    r5 .../openai-curated-remote/sites/0.1.75/skills
    r6 .../openai-curated-remote/superpowers/6.4.2/skills
    r7 .../openai-curated-remote/work-pets/0.1.6/skills
    r8 .codex/plugins/cache/openai-primary-runtime
    r9 .../openai-primary-runtime/spreadsheets/26.921.10847/skills

A `codex exec` session a few minutes later, same binary and CODEX_HOME:

    r0 .codex/skills   r1 .agents/skills   r2 .codex/skills/.system
    r3 .codex/plugins/cache/openai-bundled
    r4 .codex/plugins/cache/openai-primary-runtime
    r5 .../openai-primary-runtime/spreadsheets/26.921.10847/skills

There is no `openai-curated-remote` root, so none of the three remote-installed plugins is available. Reproduced on 4 consecutive `exec` runs. `-c 'plugins."superpowers@openai-curated-remote".enabled=true'` makes no difference. Locally configured plugins (`openai-bundled`, `openai-primary-runtime`) load fine.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?
1. Install a plugin from the curated marketplace (e.g. Superpowers via `/plugins` or the Codex app) and confirm it with `codex plugin list`.
2. Run:

       codex exec --json --sandbox read-only "Do not run commands. List the names of all skills in your instructions." < /dev/null

3. Compare the skill roots in the developer message of this run's rollout (`~/.codex/sessions/.../rollout-*.jsonl`) with those of an interactive session.

Example exec thread id: 01a1082d-df27-7cd2-bee3-d48c99785624

### What is the expected behavior?
`codex exec` loads the same enabled plugins as an interactive session. If skipping them is intentional, the docs say so and exec warns that remote-installed plugins were not loaded.

### Additional information
Likely cause (from reading `main` @ c2f7fe8, not the 0.160.0 tag):
- Remote-installed plugins come from an in-memory snapshot ([manager.rs#L563](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/c2f7fe89d87ce853900d0b5cb1f5dc4863e44d73/codex-rs/core-plugins/src/manager.rs#L563), [#L1102](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/c2f7fe89d87ce853900d0b5cb1f5dc4863e44d73/codex-rs/core-plugins/src/manager.rs#L1102)).
- Only the plugin startup tasks fill it, and they spawn the remote sync in the background ([manager.rs#L2889-L2895](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/c2f7fe89d87ce853900d0b5cb1f5dc4863e44d73/codex-rs/core-plugins/src/manager.rs#L2889-L2895)).
- `codex exec` runs an in-process app-server with `plugin_startup_tasks: Some(PluginStartupConfig::Current)` ([in_process.rs#L517](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/c2f7fe89d87ce853900d0b5cb1f5dc4863e44d73/codex-rs/app-server/src/in_process.rs#L517)) and starts its thread right away, so session init reads an empty snapshot.
- Long-lived TUI/App processes pick the plugins up once the sync completes (`on_effective_plugins_changed`).

Possible fixes: have exec wait for the remote-installed refresh (with a short timeout) before `thread/start`, or seed the snapshot from the on-disk cache, since the bundles are already in `~/.codex/plugins/cache`.

Workaround: copy the plugin's `skills/` into the repo's `.agents/skills/<plugin>/`; `codex exec` discovers those.

Related but different: #35387 (`request_plugin_install` in `codex exec`).

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using?

Codex App 26.930.31730 (bundled codex-cli 0.160.0), macOS (Apple Silicon)

### What platform is your computer?

macOS; phone: Codex Remote (mobile) over cellular

### What issue are you seeing?

On mobile, opening **any** thread on my Mac fails with "timed out loading this task's messages" — including small, idle threads.

From `~/.codex/logs_2.sqlite` (target `codex_app_server_transport::transport::remote_control::websocket`):

- The remote-control WebSocket connects, then drops **exactly ~60 s later** with `remote control websocket pong timeout`, reconnects 2 s later, and repeats (7 cycles in 10 minutes).
- Each cycle coincides with a `thread/resume` for a large **running** thread (`composing running thread resume response`). During one cycle a single chatgpt.com connection uploaded **35.9 MB in 11 minutes** and kept going.
- One trigger was not user-initiated: `thread/resume` with request id `__slingshot_backend_notification_thread_resume__:<thread-id>` auto-resumed a **2.5 GB** rollout.
- Changing the network path (two unrelated proxy routes) did not change the pattern; a parallel WebSocket ping test over the same routes had 0 drops in 10 min, so the network is not the cause.

Rollout composition of the 2.5 GB thread (728 turns):

- `compacted` records: **1.56 GB (61%)** across 144 compactions (~10.8 MB each)
- lines containing inline `data:image` base64: **2.28 GB (90%)**
- 398 single lines larger than 1 MB

So auto-compaction ran, but each compaction snapshot re-embeds the retained screenshots, and the on-disk rollout grows with every compaction (related: #32128, #33493, #40323).

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Have a long-running thread with many screenshots (hundreds of MB to GB of rollout).
2. Enable Remote Control and open that thread from mobile (or let a backend notification resume it).
3. Try to open any small thread from mobile: it times out until the large resume finishes or the app is restarted.

### What is the expected behavior?

- One thread's resume payload should not starve the shared remote-control channel (pings/pongs should not queue behind bulk data, or bulk data should use a separate stream with flow control).
- `thread/resume` over Remote Control should page recent turns (the protocol already has `thread/turns/list` / `nextCursor` / `excludeTurns`) instead of composing the full running-thread state.
- Compaction snapshots should not re-embed historical images; there should be a way to prune/compact the on-disk rollout.
- Backend-notification resumes should not auto-load multi-GB threads.

### Additional information

Workaround: archive the giant threads and restart the app.

<!-- Proposed title: [Linux/WSL2] Managed app-server cannot accept new sessions after its Unix control socket is unlinked -->

### What version of Codex CLI is running?

`codex-cli 0.160.0` (standalone Linux package, managed app-server 0.160.0).

### What platform is your computer?

WSL2, Linux `6.18.33.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2`, x86_64.

### Codex doctor report

A fresh `codex doctor --json` run after recovery reports overall `ok`, with `app_server.status`, `installation`, `mcp.config`, and `state.paths` all `ok`; no MCP servers are configured. This does not inspect the socket state at the earlier failure time. Full report can be supplied privately if useful after reviewing its paths and environment details.

### What issue are you seeing?

After sessions failed, new sessions would not start until the user deliberately ran `wsl --shutdown`. The exact UI error was not saved. During a prior observed failure, the managed app-server PID was still alive but the stable control-socket symlink under the Codex home pointed to a missing Unix socket under `/tmp/codex-daemon-<uid>/`. That makes new client connections fail while an already-accepted connection may remain open.

The transport binds its physical Unix listener and publishes the symlink at startup, but does not check whether either path remains present during the daemon's lifetime. If temporary-directory cleanup unlinks the listener path, the process can remain alive without accepting new clients through that path. A separate startup recovery change can restart a managed daemon, but a restart may interrupt active sessions.

This is a confirmed socket-lifecycle failure class. It is **not** a claim that it caused every recent TUI termination: in another concurrent run, the daemon continued serving after a TUI stopped logging, and WSLg's Weston compositor separately segfaulted. No OOM kill was found in host logs.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

A focused synthetic test of the transport primitive:

1. Start the app-server Unix control-socket acceptor and establish a WebSocket client.
2. Remove the physical socket directory entry while the listener process stays alive, as can happen when temporary storage is cleaned.
3. Start four new clients concurrently through the stable rendezvous path.
4. Separately remove the rendezvous symlink and try another new client.
5. Send a ping on the original WebSocket.

On the released transport, new clients cannot connect after step 2 until the daemon is replaced. The existing connection can survive the unlink. The candidate source change and passing regression test are visible on `RevealUIStudio/codex`, branch `fix/daemon-recover-missing-control-socket`, commit `26fb7c8`:

https://github.com/RevealUIStudio/codex/commit/26fb7c832ef8807d9dfd0f010ee37c879ccf7ef1

`cargo test -p codex-app-server-transport lost_physical_socket_recovers_without_dropping_existing_or_concurrent_clients --locked` passed (1 test, 158 filtered out). The branch is provided as root-cause evidence, in accordance with the current policy against external PRs.

### What is the expected behavior?

The managed app-server should restore a lost control-socket listener and rendezvous link without dropping existing clients, while preventing one daemon from overwriting another daemon's listener. New single and concurrent sessions should connect after the path loss.

### Additional information

Related but distinct: #50619 concerns an inherited deleted working directory causing config reload errors; #47206 concerns a stale PID record. This report concerns loss of the *physical Unix listener path while its process is still alive*. The user-initiated WSL shutdowns happened after sessions failed and were recovery actions, not the initiating failure.

- Two `configRequirements/read` requests took 201,892 and 183,474 ms. Matching native request receipts show they reached the app-server promptly. Native response logs did not provide matching completion IDs, so backend work and response-delivery delay remain distinguishable possibilities.
- `mcpServerStatus/list` took 126,306 ms. Codex Security `tools/list` timed out after 120 seconds. The window contained 30 queue-rejection and 136 discovery-failure log records; these are not counts of distinct UI stalls.
- Twelve route-aware HTTP warnings coincided with MCP `initialize` failures to `api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/` and `chatgpt.com/backend-api/ps/mcp`. They report `error_is_timeout=true`, `error_is_connect=false`. Other recorded requests to Codex endpoints returned HTTP 200 during the same period. No retained `accounts/check` request receipt identifies its outcome.

A narrow experiment disabled the direct Playwright and Chrome DevTools entries. Saved bytes were verified, but Desktop runtime adoption was unverified and the failure pattern recurred. The experiment was reversed to exact original bytes with unchanged owner/DACL. It is not a demonstrated repair or a controlled causal exclusion of those servers. No restart, forced reload, authentication change or backend override was used for that experiment. An independent CLI using `--no-daemon` continued performing captured local reads and responses.

The version-tagged routing implementation wraps configuration/requirements loading, shared discovery admission, `accounts/check`, and requirements reload in the same 15-second timeout. Current evidence does not identify which inner stage waited, nor prove invalid credentials, a network fault, a particular MCP server, or a particular chat as the root cause. Published SQLite-stall fixes are already listed for the reported 0.160.0 runtime.

Related report: #47145, but this observation concerns failures of concurrent active turns after startup, not a demonstrated login-persistence workaround.

Could maintainers provide a supported, privacy-preserving diagnostic for routing-stage timing and app-server response-delivery waits on Windows, or identify a corresponding fix? Raw credentials, conversation contents and authentication-reset experiments are intentionally outside this report.

items.title: [Windows] Canceled turn-diff captures leave over 774 GiB of tmp_pack_* files in the repository

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

items.body:
### Summary

Codex Desktop’s automatic turn-diff capture repeatedly runs `git add` against my workspace. These operations are canceled when the Git snapshot becomes stale, leaving large `tmp_pack_*` files in the repository’s `.git/objects/pack` directory.

An initial inspection found **1,838 temporary pack files totaling 774.39 GiB**. A later observation found **1,841 files totaling 775.69 GiB**, so accumulation was continuing during the investigation.

This happens without a user-requested staging or commit operation.

### Environment

- OS: Windows 10 Home, version 10.0.19045
- Installed package: `OpenAI.Codex_26.930.3930.0_x64__2p2nqsd0c76g0`
- Application executable: `ChatGPT.exe` inside that Codex package
- Workspace: a local Git repository containing documents, projects, large binary artifacts and backups
- Repository configuration already includes `gc.auto=0`

### Disk usage

| Content | Observed size |
|---|---:|
| Entire workspace | 821.91 GiB |
| `.git` directory | 790.05 GiB |
| `.git/objects/pack` | 775.64 GiB |
| 1,838 `tmp_pack_*` files | **774.39 GiB** |
| Four finalized `.pack` files | 1.25 GiB |

These are summed logical file sizes, not deduplicated allocated-size measurements. Finalized pack files do not represent the entire repository history; loose objects and LFS storage also exist.

The temporary files accumulated across multiple dates, with a sharp increase starting September 26. Files created September 27–30 alone account for approximately **568.58 GiB**.

### Observed process chain

A live process inspection captured:

```text
Codex package / app / ChatGPT.exe
  └─ Git / cmd / git.exe
      └─ Git / mingw64 / bin / git.exe
```

The Git command was:

```text
git -c safe.bareRepository=explicit
    -c core.hooksPath=NUL
    -c core.fsmonitor=
    add --sparse --pathspec-from-file=- --pathspec-file-nul
```

The parent process was the desktop application, rather than a shell command issued by the assistant during the investigation.

### Logs identify the operation and cancellation

The Git worker logs repeatedly contain:

```text
cwd=<affected repository>
requestKind=turn-diff-capture-start
source=turn_diff_analytics
subcommand=add
aborted=true
failureReason=canceled
success=false
timedOut=false
```

For example, on October 4, 2026:

| Git cancellation time, UTC | Duration |
|---|---:|
| 16:50:18.454 | 29.059 seconds |
| 16:58:30.930 | 91.096 seconds |
| 17:01:28.584 | 39.165 seconds |
| 17:05:15.687 | 94.832 seconds |

Immediately afterward, the main application log reports:

```text
Failed to start turn diff analytics capture
errorMessage="Git snapshot became stale"
```

The corresponding temporary packs’ last-write times align with these cancellations, within approximately two seconds.

### Read-only inspection of the installed application

Inspection of the installed `app.asar` shows the following path:

1. A `turn/started` listener can request `turn-diff-capture-start`, subject to feature and account conditions.
2. The worker collects working-tree changes and untracked paths.
3. It creates a temporary index and runs `git add`, followed by `git write-tree`.
4. The inspected temporary-index wrapper supplies `GIT_INDEX_FILE`, but does not supply a separate `GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY`.
5. Snapshot invalidation retires the previous snapshot and aborts its signal.
6. The Git execution path enables process-tree termination. The Windows implementation uses `taskkill.exe /pid … /t /f`.
7. The wrapper’s cleanup removes its temporary index directory. No corresponding cleanup of abandoned packs in the repository object directory was found in this path.

The inspected diff-output size limit applies after snapshot construction; it does not bound the preceding object-writing operation.

This supports the following failure mechanism:

```text
Automatic turn-diff capture
→ large untracked files are written as Git objects
→ snapshot becomes stale
→ Git is canceled
→ unfinished pack remains
→ a later capture repeats the work
```

### What the temporary packs contain

A read-only, streaming inspection of one large temporary pack confirmed that its first two objects exactly match existing workspace files:

- An older application installer: **830,566,790 bytes**
- A SQLite database in a local rollback backup: **1,195,106,304 bytes**

Both matches were verified using full SHA-256 comparisons.

Further objects matched the sizes and formats of large JSONL files in that backup. Several packs from different dates also had the same installer prefix.

The unfinished pack header reported one object, but sequential inspection found additional objects. Its header therefore should not be treated as a finalized object count.

### Observed conditions

The affected workspace contains large untracked files and is used for ordinary Codex conversations and file operations. The application’s turn-diff capture starts automatically; a manual Git staging or commit request is not required.

A minimal synthetic reproduction has **not** been performed. The evidence above comes from repeated observations in the affected workspace.

### Expected behavior

- Automatic change capture should have a bounded disk-write budget.
- Canceling a capture should not leave large temporary packs accumulating indefinitely.
- Temporary snapshot storage should be isolated and safely reclaimed after cancellation.
- Large-file limits should apply before writing objects.
- Users should have a reliable way to disable automatic Git-writing features while retaining explicitly requested Git operations.

### Related reports

- #28750 — Repeated automatic `git add` operations leave large temporary packs in the repository.
- #19588 — Automatic snapshot operations fill disk space in a broad workspace.
- #43158 — Canceled workspace-diff collection leaves temporary Git objects on macOS; a related failure class with a different storage path.

items.body:
### Update — October 11, 2026: Successful sign-in after clearing Firefox cookies

**Status on my machine:** I can now sign in to ChatGPT Classic successfully. This is a **workaround that worked for me**, not confirmation that the underlying authentication bug has been fixed for everyone.

After seeing the troubleshooting sequence shared in [this comment](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/50919#issuecomment-6114551317), I tried the following steps, in order:

1. Ended all ChatGPT Classic processes using Windows Task Manager, reopened Classic, and retried login.
2. Checked for ChatGPT Classic updates through the Microsoft Store.
3. Used **Windows Settings → Apps → Installed apps → ChatGPT Classic → Advanced options → Repair**.
4. Checked the Windows default browser settings.
5. Retried the ChatGPT Classic login flow in the browser.

**Result:** These steps **did not fix the problem**. I still could not log in to Classic.

I then tried one additional step:

6. In **Firefox**, cleared the stored cookies/site data associated with ChatGPT/OpenAI sign-in (via **Settings → Privacy & Security → Cookies and Site Data → Manage Data**), then retried signing in to Classic.

**Result:** The login worked immediately, and **I am now signed in to ChatGPT Classic**.

The key difference in my successful attempt was **clearing the browser cookies**; the preceding troubleshooting sequence had not worked on its own. I cannot confirm exactly which cookie or session state was responsible, or whether the same workaround will fix the issue for other users or browsers.

**Note:** The original report below describes the behavior **before this workaround**. I'm leaving the issue open because other users have reproduced it and the root cause has not been established.

---

### What issue are you seeing?

Before applying the workaround above, I was unable to sign in specifically to **ChatGPT Classic on Windows**.

When I initiate login from ChatGPT Classic, the browser authentication flow appears to complete successfully, but the callback reaches a URL similar to:

`https://chatgpt.com/api/auth/callback/openai-sidetron?code=...`

and displays:

`Error: This action with HTTP GET is not supported by NextAuth.js`

ChatGPT Classic does not complete authentication.

This appears to affect **ChatGPT Classic specifically**. Using the same OpenAI account, I am able to successfully authenticate and use:

- ChatGPT on the web
- Codex
- The newer ChatGPT Windows app with the ChatGPT/Codex switcher

I have not encountered this login failure in those clients.

This appears related to previously reported `openai-sidetron` / NextAuth callback problems, including #48960 and the still-open #50318. However, the reports I have found appear to concern the newer ChatGPT/Codex desktop application.

I have not found an existing report where **ChatGPT Classic fails while the newer ChatGPT app, Codex, and ChatGPT Web all continue to authenticate successfully**, so this may be a ChatGPT Classic-specific variant of the same underlying issue.

There is also unusual application behavior after the authentication failure. The visible ChatGPT Classic window may disappear from the desktop and taskbar, making the application appear closed. However, Task Manager continues to show `ChatGPT Classic (5)` as a running application.

The application may later become visible again without me manually relaunching it.

Additionally, the same failed `openai-sidetron` callback page will occasionally open in my browser again even though I have not manually initiated another login attempt.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Launch ChatGPT Classic on Windows while signed out.
2. Select the option to sign in.
3. Complete the authentication process in the browser normally.
4. Allow the browser to redirect to the ChatGPT authentication callback.
5. The callback reaches `/api/auth/callback/openai-sidetron?code=...`.
6. Instead of returning authentication to ChatGPT Classic, the browser displays:

   `Error: This action with HTTP GET is not supported by NextAuth.js`

7. ChatGPT Classic remains unauthenticated.
8. In some attempts, the visible ChatGPT Classic window disappears from the desktop/taskbar afterward.
9. Open Task Manager and observe that `ChatGPT Classic (5)` is still listed as a running application despite no visible ChatGPT Classic window.
10. In some cases, ChatGPT Classic later becomes visible again without being manually relaunched.
11. The same callback/error page may also reopen in the browser later without another login attempt being manually initiated.

For comparison, on the same machine and using the same OpenAI account:

- ChatGPT Web authenticates successfully.
- Codex authenticates successfully.
- The newer ChatGPT Windows app with the ChatGPT/Codex switcher authenticates successfully.

Before the workaround, the failure was reproducible only with ChatGPT Classic on this machine.

### What is the expected behavior?

After browser authentication completes successfully, the `openai-sidetron` callback should return authentication control to ChatGPT Classic and sign the user into the application.

If authentication fails, ChatGPT Classic should remain visibly open and display an appropriate login error or retry option.

The application should not disappear from desktop/taskbar visibility while continuing to run in the background, and the authentication callback should not appear to reopen later without another login attempt being initiated.

### Additional information

Related issues:

- #48960
- #50318

The callback path and NextAuth.js error appear to be the same or very similar to those reports.

The main difference in this case is that the issue appears isolated to **ChatGPT Classic**.

Authentication status **before the workaround**, using the same OpenAI account:

- ChatGPT Web: Working
- Codex: Working
- New ChatGPT Windows app with ChatGPT/Codex switcher: Working
- ChatGPT Classic: Fails to authenticate

Observed error:

`Error: This action with HTTP GET is not supported by NextAuth.js`

Observed callback path:

`/api/auth/callback/openai-sidetron`

After the failed login, Task Manager may continue to show:

`ChatGPT Classic (5)`

even when there is no visible ChatGPT Classic window or taskbar entry.

Because the application can later reappear and the authentication callback page may reopen without another manually initiated login attempt, it is possible that ChatGPT Classic remains running in the background and retries or re-triggers part of the authentication flow. I cannot confirm the cause of that behavior.

Screenshots of the callback error and application/process state can be provided or attached.

labels.name: bug

items.body:
## Summary

Microsoft Office COM automation hangs when executed by Codex under the native Windows `:workspace` / unelevated restricted-token sandbox.

Both `Access.Application` and `Excel.Application` successfully launch their Office executable (`MSACCESS.EXE` / `EXCEL.EXE`), but COM activation never returns to the caller.

The same Access/ACE environment works outside the Codex sandbox under the same Windows user. This appears to be a regression: Access/DAO automation had been used successfully from Codex during normal development for several weeks before the recent failure.

## Environment

- Windows 10 Pro, build 26300, x64
- Codex CLI/runtime: `0.160.0`
- Codex Desktop/App Windows package: `26.930.3930.0`
- Permission profile: `:workspace`
- `[windows] sandbox = "unelevated"`
- Medium integrity, Session 1
- `IsTokenRestricted=True`
- Restricted SID count: 5
- AppContainer: False
- Microsoft Office / Access: 64-bit Office 16.x
- Access version observed: `16.0.20430.20092`

## Minimal Access reproduction

Inside Codex `:workspace`:

```powershell
$app = New-Object -ComObject Access.Application
```

Observed:

```text
ACCESS ACTIVATION BEGIN
Activation returned: False
TIMEOUT after ~15130 ms
New MSACCESS.EXE created: True
Session: 1
MSACCESS remained alive during wait: True
```

No ACCDB was opened and no UI automation occurred.

## Minimal Excel reproduction

```powershell
$excel = New-Object -ComObject Excel.Application
```

Observed:

```text
EXCEL ACTIVATION BEGIN
Activation returned: False
TIMEOUT after ~15120 ms
New EXCEL.EXE created: True
Session: 1
EXCEL remained alive during wait: True
```

No workbook was opened or created.

## Control matrix

| Component | Server type | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Scripting.Dictionary | Generic InProc COM | PASS |
| Data Exchange Host | Windows LocalServer COM | PASS |
| Runtime Broker | Windows LocalServer COM | TIMEOUT |
| Excel.Application | Office LocalServer COM | TIMEOUT |
| Access.Application | Office LocalServer COM | TIMEOUT |
| DAO.DBEngine.120 | ACE InProc COM | TIMEOUT |
| Access ODBC | ACE/ODBC | TIMEOUT |

The successful Data Exchange Host activation shows that LocalServer COM activation is not universally broken under this restricted token.

## Access child token

During blocked `Access.Application` activation, the newly launched `MSACCESS.EXE` was inspected read-only. Controller, PowerShell worker, and MSACCESS were all Medium integrity, Session 1, restricted, and carried the same five restricted SIDs. Office therefore executes inside the restricted-token boundary.

## DAO / ODBC evidence

Activation-only `DAO.DBEngine.120` hangs after ~15 seconds without opening a database.

For Access ODBC, the native Node ODBC module loads and `ACEODBC.DLL` is loaded, but `odbc.connect()` blocks indefinitely.

The same ODBC test against an intentionally nonexistent ACCDB also hangs instead of returning a missing-file/database error, indicating the failure occurs before meaningful opening of the target database.

## Static accessibility controls

Under the actual Codex restricted token, read access succeeds for the target ACCDB, `odbc.node`, `MSACCESS.EXE`, `ACEDAO.DLL`, `ACEODBC.DLL`, relevant Access/DAO/ODBC registry registrations, TEMP enumeration, and workspace enumeration.

This does not appear to be a simple inability to read Office binaries or the database.

## Private-desktop control

The identical Node/Access ODBC workload was launched on a newly created private desktop while retaining a normal unrestricted Windows token:

```text
ODBC LOAD SUCCESS
CONNECT SUCCESS
SELECT 1 SUCCESS
COUNT SUCCESS
WorkOrderCount: 333
CLOSE SUCCESS
```

Private-desktop execution alone therefore does not reproduce the failure.

## Privilege-removal control

A token created with `DISABLE_MAX_PRIVILEGE` but without restricting SIDs also completed the Access ODBC workload successfully (count 333). Simple privilege removal therefore does not reproduce the problem.

## Outside-Codex A/B control

The historical Access ODBC test was run outside Codex using the same Windows user, exact Codex-bundled Node executable, same Node ODBC package, same Access ODBC driver, same connection string, and same ACCDB:

```text
ODBC CONNECTION SUCCEEDED
WorkOrderCount: 333
```

This isolates the failure to the Codex execution/security context rather than Node, ACE installation, ODBC package, connection string, database, or Windows account.

## Security-context comparison

Successful normal Windows process:

```text
Integrity: Medium
Administrators: DENY_ONLY
IsTokenRestricted: False
Restricted SID count: 0
```

Failing Codex process:

```text
Integrity: Medium
Administrators: DENY_ONLY
IsTokenRestricted: True
Restricted SID count: 5
```

Ordinary group membership is otherwise substantially the same.

## Expected behavior

Office COM automation should either return the automation object or a meaningful COM error. It should not launch the Office executable and then block indefinitely.

## Suspected area

The evidence suggests an incompatibility between the current Codex Windows restricted-token sandbox and initialization/IPC used by Microsoft Office/ACE. Restricted-SID/default-DACL behavior may be relevant for COM/RPC/IPC objects, but this specific root cause is not yet proven.

## Regression significance

This workflow previously worked during normal Codex-assisted Microsoft Access development. The regression prevents normal read-only Access/DAO inspection under `:workspace`. Full Access works, but is undesirable for routine development.

## Request

Please investigate whether the current Windows restricted-token construction/default DACL prevents Microsoft Office COM servers from completing COM/RPC initialization.

Useful regression tests inside the native Windows `:workspace` sandbox:

```powershell
$excel = New-Object -ComObject Excel.Application
$excel.Version
$excel.Quit()
```

and:

```powershell
$access = New-Object -ComObject Access.Application
$access.Version
$access.Quit()
```

Both currently launch their Office executable but hang before returning the COM object.

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

26.930.41038 (Microsoft Store package OpenAI.Codex 26.930.4958.0)

### What subscription do you have?

Pro

### What platform is your computer?

Windows 11 Pro build 26300.9457 (Insider build), x64. Security software: ESET Internet Security 19.2.10.0. `[windows] sandbox = "elevated"` (default).

### What issue are you seeing?

I uninstalled the Windows app, moved the old `%USERPROFILE%\.codex` folder away, and installed the app again. After that, every shell command fails before it starts:

```
exec_command failed: CreateProcess { message: "Rejected(\"Failed to create unified exec process: helper_unknown_error: setup refresh had errors\")" }
```

File edits still work. Commands worked on the same machine before the reinstall.

Sandbox log (`%USERPROFILE%\.codex\.sandbox\sandbox.<date>.log`):

```
granting write ACE to C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\Temp for sandbox group and capability SID
write ACE grant failed on C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\Temp: SetSecurityInfo failed: 5
setup refresh completed with errors: ["write ACE failed on C:\\Users\\<user>\\AppData\\Local\\Temp: SetSecurityInfo failed: 5"]
setup error: setup refresh had errors
```

In the same run, the write ACEs for the workspace folder and for `.codex\...` were granted successfully. Only `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp` failed.

**Tests on this PC strongly suggest that ESET's HIPS-related protection blocks the DACL change on the Temp folder itself.** I checked this on one PC running a Windows Insider build. Other environments were not tested, and not every other factor was ruled out.

- The user owns Temp and has Full Control. The folder can be opened with WRITE_DAC, but writing the DACL is denied:
  - .NET `Directory.SetAccessControl`: UnauthorizedAccessException
  - `NtSetSecurityObject` (DACL only, no inheritance propagation): `0xC0000022` STATUS_ACCESS_DENIED. Same result from an elevated PowerShell.
- The same call succeeds on subfolders of Temp. Only Temp itself is denied.
- Pausing ESET's real-time file system protection did not change the result.
- As a diagnostic experiment, with the network cable unplugged, I disabled HIPS for a short time. With HIPS disabled, the same non-elevated `NtSetSecurityObject` call succeeded (`0x00000000`), which added the ACE for the new capability SID to Temp.
- I then turned HIPS back on and rebooted. Commands now run in the sandbox with HIPS enabled, because the ACE stays on Temp and setup no longer needs to write it.

What I observed about the SID: after the old `.codex` was moved away and recreated, a new capability SID was created (in the new `%USERPROFILE%\.codex\cap_sid`), and setup tried to add an ACE for this new SID to Temp. Temp also has ACEs for 4 other existing capability SIDs that were added earlier. I did not test whether a reinstall alone (keeping `.codex`) creates a new SID.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Reproduced only on this one PC:

1. Windows 11 (Insider build 26300) with ESET Internet Security, HIPS enabled (default).
2. Uninstall the Codex app, move `%USERPROFILE%\.codex` away, then install the app again. A new `.codex\cap_sid` is created.
3. Open a local project and ask Codex to run any command (e.g. `dir`).
4. The command fails with `helper_unknown_error: setup refresh had errors`. The sandbox log shows `SetSecurityInfo failed: 5` on `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp`.

### What is the expected behavior?

- A solution that works with ESET HIPS kept enabled and the sandbox isolation kept intact. Disabling HIPS is not an acceptable workaround, because it also turns off other ESET protections.
- An official way to recover from this state without weakening the sandbox (for example, a documented repair step).
- The UI should show which path failed and the Win32 error, not only "setup refresh had errors". With the real path, users can see that a security product may be involved.
- If HIPS-type products are known to conflict with the Windows sandbox setup, a short note in the docs would help.

### Additional information

- The HIPS experiment above was done only to find the cause. It is not a workaround I recommend, and I would like a fix that works with HIPS enabled.
- An ESET HIPS exclusion rule for the Codex sandbox processes was not tested.
- File system minifilters loaded: bindflt, FsDepends, UCPD, wtd, eamonm (ESET), storqosflt, gameflt, CldFlt, bfs, FileCrypt, luafv, UnionFS, npsvctrig, Wof, FileInfo.
- Possibly related (same error text; I have not confirmed they share this cause): #44882, #50772, #31620, #44309. Capability SID change after sandbox reinit: #46213.

items.body:
## Summary

On Windows, Codex's MXC sandbox fails before launching any child process when an unrelated BitLocker data volume is present but locked.

The project/workspace is on another drive and does not reference the locked volume.

## Environment

- Windows 11 build 26200
- ChatGPT/Codex Desktop: 26.930.3930.0
- bundled codex-cli: 0.160.0
- Windows sandbox backend: MXC

## Reproduction

With an unrelated BitLocker data volume locked (observed as `E:\`), run any trivial command through MXC, for example a command that only writes a fixed string from a workspace on another drive.

The command never starts. MXC exits first with:

```text
MXC launcher: enumerate MXC volume E:\: This drive is locked by BitLocker Drive Encryption. You must unlock this drive from Control Panel. (os error -2144272384)
```

The signed error value corresponds to `0x80310000` / `FVE_E_LOCKED_VOLUME`.

## Root cause

In `codex-rs/mxc-sandbox/src/policy.rs`, a permission profile containing `:root` is materialized across logical volume roots returned by `GetLogicalDrives()`.

The generated root for the locked BitLocker volume is probed with `read_dir()`. The resulting `FVE_E_LOCKED_VOLUME` error is not classified by `inaccessible_volume()` as an unavailable volume, so the failure falls through to `PolicyError::EnumerateVolume` and MXC exits before child-process creation.

Current upstream appears to retain the same omission.

A named MXC permission profile without `:root` avoids the failure on the same host, which isolates the trigger to generated root-volume expansion rather than general MXC process launch.

## Expected behavior

An unrelated locked BitLocker volume should be treated like another unavailable logical volume during generated volume-root expansion and should not prevent commands scoped to accessible volumes from launching.

Explicitly requested paths should continue to fail closed.

## Suggested fix

Treat `FVE_E_LOCKED_VOLUME` (`0x80310000`) as an inaccessible/unavailable volume in the generated logical-volume expansion path.

A minimal Windows regression test could assert that:

```rust
io::Error::from_raw_os_error(0x80310000u32 as i32)
```

is classified as an inaccessible volume, while an unrelated filesystem error remains fatal.

This should preserve the existing fail-closed behavior for explicit path grants while preventing an unrelated locked BitLocker volume from breaking all MXC command execution.

### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

26.930.31730

### What subscription do you have?

ChatGPT Plus

### What platform is your computer?

Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.26300.0 64 bits

### What issue are you seeing?

Summary
ChatGPT/Codex Desktop for Windows shares the default Codex home directory (%USERPROFILE%\.codex) with Codex CLI. After configuring DeepSeek as a third-party provider in the default Codex home, the Desktop app unexpectedly inherited that provider configuration.

Observed behavior
On Desktop version 26.930.31730:
- DeepSeek-V4-Pro appeared as the active model/provider inside the Desktop app.
- My normal OpenAI models disappeared.
- My OpenAI account was no longer shown normally.
- My regular ChatGPT conversations disappeared from the Desktop app.
- The app effectively behaved as though the third-party Codex provider had replaced the normal ChatGPT/Work environment.
- My account, subscription, OpenAI models, and conversations continued to work normally on chatgpt.com.
I also confirmed that Codex background processes such as codex-windows-sandbox-service.exe and extension-host.exe were actively holding files under %USERPROFILE%\.codex.

Reproduction
1. Start with ChatGPT Desktop and Codex CLI using the default %USERPROFILE%\.codex.
2. Configure a third-party model provider such as DeepSeek in the default Codex home.
3. Fully restart ChatGPT Desktop.
4. The Desktop app may inherit the third-party provider and no longer present the normal authenticated OpenAI experience.

Recovery
I backed up the Codex directory and restored the pre-DeepSeek configuration using the provider's uninstall/restore procedure.
The third-party configuration had modified the shared Codex home, including config.toml and a provider-specific models.json.
Expected behavior
Configuring a third-party provider for Codex CLI should not unexpectedly hide or replace the authenticated OpenAI account, models, ChatGPT conversations, or normal ChatGPT/Work experience in the Desktop app.

Suggested safeguard
Since Desktop and native Codex intentionally share the same CODEX_HOME, please consider:
- warning users when a third-party provider is configured in the default Codex home;
- recommending an isolated CODEX_HOME for third-party providers;
- providing separate configuration profiles for Desktop and CLI;
- or preventing an external CLI provider from obscuring the normal authenticated OpenAI Desktop experience.
A warning such as:
“Third-party providers configured in the primary Codex home may also affect ChatGPT Desktop. Consider using an isolated CODEX_HOME.”
would have prevented this issue.

Environment
- Windows 11
- ChatGPT/Codex Desktop: 26.930.31730
- Subscription: ChatGPT Plus
- Default Codex home: %USERPROFILE%\.codex
- Third-party provider: DeepSeek V4 Pro
I can also provide a Desktop /feedback session ID if useful.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?
1. Install and sign in to ChatGPT/Codex Desktop for Windows.
2. Ensure the default Codex home is %USERPROFILE%\.codex.
3. Configure a third-party Codex provider such as DeepSeek in that default Codex home, modifying config.toml and adding the provider-specific model configuration.
4. Fully quit the Desktop app, including the tray/background process.
5. Reopen the Desktop app.
6. Observe that the app inherits the third-party provider configuration:
   - DeepSeek-V4-Pro appears as the active model/provider.
   - OpenAI models are no longer shown.
   - the normal OpenAI account UI is missing or altered.
   - regular ChatGPT conversations are not shown in the Desktop app.
7. Verify that the same OpenAI account, subscription, and conversations still work normally on chatgpt.com.
8. Restore/remove the third-party configuration from the shared .codex directory and restart the Desktop app.
9. The normal OpenAI experience returns.
This reproduces the issue when the Desktop app and CLI share the same default CODEX_HOME.

### What is the expected behavior?

ChatGPT/Codex Desktop should preserve the normal authenticated OpenAI experience even when Codex CLI is configured with a third-party provider.
In particular:
- my OpenAI account should remain visible and authenticated;
- my normal ChatGPT conversations should continue to appear in the Desktop app;
- OpenAI models should remain available;
- third-party providers configured for CLI use should not silently replace or hide the normal ChatGPT/Work experience;
- if the Desktop app intentionally shares the same CODEX_HOME, it should either isolate Desktop from external providers or clearly warn the user before a third-party provider can affect the Desktop app.
Ideally, external providers should require an isolated CODEX_HOME or explicit opt-in for Desktop use.

### Additional information

The issue was limited to the Windows Desktop app. My OpenAI account, subscription, models, and conversations continued to work normally on chatgpt.com.
I confirmed that the Desktop app and Codex background processes were actively using %USERPROFILE%\.codex, including codex-windows-sandbox-service.exe and extension-host.exe.
Restoring the pre-DeepSeek Codex configuration removed the third-party provider settings. I also backed up the original .codex directory before making changes.
This behavior is especially risky because users configuring third-party providers for CLI experimentation may not realize that the same Codex home is also consumed by the Desktop app.
Recommended mitigation: explicitly document and warn that third-party providers should use a separate CODEX_HOME, and/or provide separate Desktop and CLI profiles.

### What issue are you seeing?

## Summary

In long-running Codex sessions, I am seeing generated natural-language text inside tool-call arguments intermittently lose spaces between words.

For example, an agent intended to communicate text equivalent to:

```text
current typed growth is only 8 MiB raw, all other categories 0.
```

but generated:

```text
current typed growth is only8MiB raw, allothercategories0.
```

This is not only a rendering issue. The malformed text is already present in the `response_item` stored in the Codex session JSONL, before the MCP tool is executed.

I have also noticed once similar missing-space/concatenation behavior in a Markdown files generated by agents. But it's been overwritten so no example.

The same generated message contains several other apparent concatenations:

```text
nowfailed
late8MiB
fullcensus
holdnewregistrations
finalgrant
checkpointheadroom18.3GB/free1.018TB
```

Immediately afterward, `item_completed` contains the same malformed text in the arguments passed to `send_message_to_thread`.

This suggests the spaces are already missing when the tool call is generated, rather than being removed by `send_message_to_thread`, MCP serialization, session persistence, or TUI rendering.

Interestingly, a shell command generated as part of the same tool invocation appears normally spaced, so this does not look like indiscriminate whitespace stripping from the JSON/tool transport.

## Expected behavior

Generated natural-language tool arguments should preserve normal word spacing, e.g.:

```text
current typed growth is only 8 MiB raw, all other categories 0.
```

## Actual behavior

Some spaces disappear, resulting in concatenated words/tokens:

```text
current typed growth is only8MiB raw, allothercategories0.
```

The issue appears intermittent. I have noticed it particularly in agent-to-agent messages and generated Markdown, while normal messages from Codex to me appear correctly spaced.

## Evidence from session JSONL

The important sequence is:

1. `response_item` contains a `custom_tool_call`.
2. Its generated `input` already contains the malformed text.
3. The following `item_completed` event passes the same malformed text to the MCP tool unchanged.

Therefore, the corruption appears to occur at or before generation of the tool-call input, rather than during tool execution or rendering.

## Reproduction

I do not yet have a minimal deterministic reproduction.

Observed conditions:

- Long-running Codex session
- Multi-agent workflow
- Agents communicating using `send_message_to_thread`
- Natural-language text generated inside tool-call arguments
- Similar behavior observed in some generated Markdown files

It may be related to long context/session length, but I have not confirmed that correlation yet.

### What issue are you seeing?

ChatGPT web displays an outdated PDF after the file is updated at the same path
Summary
In ChatGPT web, a user repeatedly received or viewed an earlier PDF version after the assistant updated the document and provided a link using the same filename and sandbox path. The assistant verified that the local PDF contained the requested text, while the user's screenshot showed the previous text.
The document update operations reported success. Creating a separately named copy produced a new file and link, but the user has not yet confirmed whether that resolved the display issue.
Environment
- Product: ChatGPT web, Work Mode / Codex-assisted file generation
- Date: October 4, 2026
- User timezone: America/Toronto
- File type: PDF, two pages, generated using ReportLab
- Delivery: clickable sandbox file link; file also saved through ChatGPT Library
- Browser/version and operating system: not captured for this reproduction
Steps observed
1. Generate a PDF and provide it to the user as a downloadable file.
2. Update a paragraph in the same PDF, keeping the filename and local path unchanged.
3. Regenerate the PDF and confirm the changed text through PDF text extraction and rendered page inspection.
4. Replace the existing Library document. The operation reports success and advances its version.
5. Provide a sandbox link using the same filename/path as before.
6. The user reports that the updated phrase is missing.
7. The user supplies a screenshot showing the earlier paragraph, including other sentences that had already been revised.
8. Inspect the local PDF again: it contains the new phrase and revised sentences.
9. Repeating the same link does not resolve the user's report; the user again says the change is missing.
Minimal reproduction to try
1. Create example.pdf containing Document revision A.
2. Open it using the file link in ChatGPT web.
3. Replace its content with Document revision B, preserving the same filename and sandbox path, and save the replacement to the same Library item.
4. Verify locally that the PDF contains revision B.
5. Send the same sandbox link again and open it in the web interface.
6. Check whether the preview and downloaded bytes both reflect revision B.
This minimal reproduction is proposed for engineering validation; it has not been independently executed.
Expected behavior
After a successful replacement, a newly provided link should resolve to the current document version. The preview and downloaded PDF should agree with that version. If a link intentionally references an older immutable version, the UI should make the version clear and provide access to the latest one.
Actual behavior
The user saw an earlier paragraph despite the regenerated local PDF containing the edit and the Library replacement reporting success. A screenshot corroborates that the user-facing content was older than the inspected local content.
It is not established whether the stale content originated in the PDF preview, downloaded attachment, sandbox-link resolution, Library version selection, or another delivery layer. No network trace, browser cache inspection, or hash of the user's downloaded PDF was collected.
Evidence from this session
- Local text extraction confirmed the requested phrase existed on page one.
- Rendered page inspection showed the corrected paragraph in the local PDF.
- Library replacement operations reported success, with successive versions recorded.
- The user's screenshot showed the previous wording and several other superseded sentences.
- The user reported the mismatch more than once after receiving links with the same path.
- A copy with a new filename was subsequently created and saved successfully as a new Library item.
The original document is a personal resume. It is intentionally not attached to this public-ready report. A sanitized test PDF is preferable for reproduction.
Workaround attempted
Create a copy under a distinct filename, save it as a new file, and provide a new link. The assistant verified that the copy contained the edit. User confirmation that the new link displayed the corrected content is still pending.
Impact
- Users cannot reliably tell whether an edit has been applied.
- They may submit an outdated document despite being told it was corrected.
- Repeated verification and regeneration create confusion and reduce trust.
Possible investigation areas (hypotheses, not confirmed causes)
- Whether preview caches are keyed only by filename/path rather than file revision or content identity.
- Whether sandbox links retain the original attachment mapping after a local file is overwritten.
- Whether replacement versions propagate consistently to preview and download endpoints.
- Whether existing preview sessions refresh after a document replacement.
Suggested acceptance checks
- Updating a PDF at the same path shows the new content through a newly provided link.
- Previewed and downloaded content correspond to the same document version.
- Replacing a Library item refreshes the relevant file mapping or exposes an explicit version-specific link.
- Behavior is verified both with an existing preview open and with the file reopened afterward.
Report status
Prepared from a user-observed incident. Not submitted to a GitHub repository. Root cause and exact affected delivery component remain unconfirmed.

### Summary
The Windows Codex desktop app repeatedly disappears or reloads during normal use. When the user clicks the app again, it often opens on the **New Chat** screen instead of returning to the previously viewed conversation. The issue continued on 2026-10-04 after a successful Windows package repair/registration event.

### Environment
- Windows 11 Pro, build 26200, x64
- Codex / ChatGPT desktop MSIX package: `OpenAI.Codex 26.930.4958.0`
- Desktop log build number: `13022`
- `ChatGPT.exe` version in Windows hang events: `154.0.8037.98`

### User-observed behavior
1. Use the desktop app normally in an existing chat.
2. The view/window disappears unexpectedly.
3. Click the app to reopen or return to it.
4. The app often shows **New Chat** rather than restoring the active chat.

This happens repeatedly. The user observed it again while the issue was being investigated. No deterministic trigger has been established.

### Verified local evidence (2026-10-04, Europe/Berlin local time)

items.body:
### What variant of Codex are you using?

ChatGPT iOS app + ChatGPT Desktop app on macOS, using Remote Control.

This request is specifically about the **native ChatGPT mobile app talking directly to the native ChatGPT Desktop app**. It does **not** require Codex CLI, SSH, or `app-server proxy`.

### What feature would you like to see?

## Summary

Please add a **direct-first transport** for Remote Control.

When the iPhone and desktop can already reach each other over the same LAN or a private network such as Tailscale/WireGuard, ChatGPT should prefer a direct authenticated connection between the two devices. If a direct connection cannot be established, it should automatically fall back to the existing OpenAI-hosted Remote Control path.

Conceptually:

```text
Preferred:

ChatGPT iOS
    |
    | LAN / Tailscale / WireGuard
    v
ChatGPT Desktop

Fallback:

ChatGPT iOS
    |
    v
OpenAI Remote Control relay
    |
    v
ChatGPT Desktop
```

## Motivation

I often use ChatGPT Remote Control from my iPhone while my phone and Mac are already connected to the same Tailscale network.

In that situation, the devices already have low-latency private reachability, but Remote Control still appears to use the hosted remote path. This adds avoidable latency and makes the mobile control experience feel slower than a direct connection should be.

A direct path would be especially useful for:

- low-latency steering and approvals;
- faster thread/UI updates;
- faster reconnects after briefly backgrounding the iOS app;
- users whose desktop is geographically far from the OpenAI relay path but close over a private VPN;
- reducing dependence on the relay when both paired devices are already mutually reachable.

This request is only about the **device-to-device Remote Control transport**. Model requests can continue to go to OpenAI normally.

## Proposed behavior

A possible flow:

1. Keep the existing authenticated device pairing.
2. Exchange candidate network addresses for the paired devices.
3. Try a direct encrypted connection over reachable LAN/private-VPN addresses.
4. If direct connectivity succeeds, use it for Remote Control traffic.
5. If it fails, automatically fall back to the hosted relay.

An optional transport setting could be useful:

```text
Remote Control transport

- Automatic (direct first, relay fallback)
- Direct only
- Hosted relay only
```

It would also be helpful for the UI to show whether the current connection is **Direct** or **Relayed**.

The feature should not require Tailscale specifically. Tailscale is only one common example. The same mechanism could work for normal LAN connectivity, WireGuard, IPv6, or other private networks.

### Additional information

Related issues:

- #31991 has a similar goal, but its workaround uses **SSH + Tailscale + app-server proxy**. This request is for a first-class **native ChatGPT iOS app ↔ native ChatGPT Desktop app** connection with no CLI or SSH setup.
- #23482 reports Remote Control becoming slow or unusable while Tailscale connectivity to the same host remains responsive.
- #37997 reports 10+ second reconnects from the ChatGPT iOS app after brief backgrounding.
- #35812 proposes direct trusted-device transfer for local Work chats, but that is replication/sync rather than Remote Control.

The main goal here is to make the existing paired-device Remote Control experience use the shortest available network path automatically.

labels.name: documentation
labels.description: Improvements or additions to documentation

items.body:
### What is the type of issue?

Documentation is incorrect

### What is the issue?

`codex-rs/memories/README.md` makes two stale claims about how the memory write path is triggered and where it lives.

**1. "Runtime orchestration for Phase 1 and Phase 2 still lives in `codex-core` under `codex-rs/core/src/memories/`."**

That directory no longer exists. Orchestration lives in `codex-memories-write` under `codex-rs/memories/write/src/` (`start.rs`, `phase1.rs`, `phase2.rs`), which matches that crate's own doc comment ("This crate owns the startup memory pipeline, ...").

**2. "The pipeline is triggered when a root session starts, and only if: ..."**

The trigger moved from thread lifecycle events to user turns in #19970. Today the only non-test call site of `codex_memories_write::start_memories_startup_task` is the app-server turn processor, in `turn_start_inner`:

https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/550eb50545a78468a09ce86b82426338640ef22d/codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/turn_processor.rs#L686-L699

So the pipeline starts after a `turn/start` request with non-empty input starts a new turn (`turn_has_input && started`). A request that only steers an already-active turn does not trigger it, and neither does creating, loading, or forking a thread. The call is also gated on `config_snapshot.is_primary_environment_configured()`, which the README's condition list does not mention.

The remaining listed conditions (not ephemeral, memory feature enabled, not a sub-agent session, state DB available) still match `start_memories_startup_task`.

**Suggested fix**

A README-only change is on my fork, in case it is useful as a reference: https://github.com/Melvillian/codex/commit/3d52e18cb7e19f946dc6458cdbe3d340b2f3dce8

It rewrites the intro sentence to point at `codex-rs/memories/write/src/`, adds the startup pipeline to the `codex-memories-write` crate description, and replaces the "When it runs" lead-in with:

> The pipeline is triggered from user turns, not from session or thread lifecycle events. The only call site is the app-server turn processor (`codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/turn_processor.rs`), which calls `codex_memories_write::start_memories_startup_task` after a `turn/start` request with non-empty input starts a new turn. A request that only steers an already-active turn does not trigger it.
>
> The pipeline then runs only if:
>
> - the thread's primary environment, if any, is configured
> - the session is not ephemeral
> - ...

### Where did you find it?

https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/550eb50545a78468a09ce86b82426338640ef22d/codex-rs/memories/README.md?plain=1#L5-L6

ChatGPT / Codex desktop app `26.930.31730`, build `12947`, verified from the installed app bundle. This concerns Dot coordination and the first-party `codex-app-tools` thread messaging tool, not a user application's implementation.

### What subscription do you have?

ChatGPT Pro (user-reported). No evidence currently links the failure to subscription eligibility or exhausted quota.

### What platform is your computer?

macOS 26.4.1 (25E253), Apple Silicon.

`uname -mprs`: `Darwin 25.4.0 arm64 arm`

### What issue are you seeing?

A cloud-based Dot delegates a user-requested message to an execution session with access to the official local Codex thread tools. That execution session can discover/read the intended existing local thread, but its harmless receipt-test call to `mcp__codex_app__send_message_to_thread` fails. The execution session reports that automatic approval does not recognize the human authorization relayed through the delegation.

Retained observations on October 4, 2026, retrieved through the official thread reader:

| Sender turn start (UTC) | Destination | Recorded send result | Delivery evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 02:50:50 | Original local development thread | `status: completed`, `durationMs: 881`; execution session reports a successful tool response | Subsequent reads did not show the message or an acknowledgment at that time. Acceptance only; delivery not established. |
| 14:35:04 | Newly forked local thread | `status: failed`, `durationMs: 0` | No successful acceptance or acknowledgment observed. |
| 14:46:16 | Same fork as the preceding test | `status: failed`, `durationMs: 0` | No successful acceptance or acknowledgment observed. |

For the two failed calls, the execution session reported:

- The user's authorization existed only in delegated/relayed content and was not accepted as trusted direct user authorization.
- A later same-tool retry, after the user explicitly requested another attempt, was again rejected; the session reported that review treated it as bypassing the previous denial.

The later delegation included timestamped quotations of the user's instructions, but that did not establish recognized authorization.

**Evidence boundary:** The official reader exposes the failed tool markers and the execution session's explanations, but not the original reviewer error/reason payload. The approval explanation above is therefore the executor's report, not an independently retrieved raw reviewer verdict.

The bounded prompt requested a fixed receipt phrase and the current workspace directory, with explicit instructions not to change files, run commands, or operate the GUI. No private workspace directory or result is included here.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

This is a retained observation sequence, not a claim of deterministic reproduction on every account:

1. Connect the computer containing an existing local Codex task to Dot.
2. In the Dot conversation, explicitly request a harmless receipt test to a specific existing local task.
3. Dot delegates that request to an execution session with the first-party local thread tools.
4. Confirm the intended destination through official list/read tools.
5. The execution session calls the official messaging tool with the identified thread and `hostId: "local"`, for example with this sanitized equivalent:
   ```json
   {
     "hostId": "local",
     "threadId": "<existing-local-thread-id>",
     "prompt": "Please reply only with a receipt acknowledgment and your current workspace directory. Do not modify files, run commands, or operate the GUI."
   }
   ```
6. Inspect the send result and target readback. In the observed attempts, send was recorded as failed and the executor reported missing trusted authorization.
7. A subsequent user-requested same-tool retry also failed despite relayed quotations of that confirmation.

### What is the expected behavior?

Please clarify and support the authorization flow for **cloud Dot → execution session → existing local Codex task**.

If scoped user authorization is intended to travel through native delegation, preserve its trusted provenance for approval review. If direct user consent in the execution session is required instead, expose a clear, usable approval mechanism identifying the exact action and destination. Repeated confirmations forwarded through the same channel should not be the only offered recovery path.

This request is for a supported authorization path and actionable diagnostics, not disabled safety checks or blanket permission.

### Additional information

- The earlier accepted call used a different target, execution session, and message content. It is not a controlled comparison.
- No app version change has been established; this report does **not** claim a confirmed version regression.
- A separate cloud-route lookup failure was observed earlier. Local thread reads succeeding means that lookup failure alone does not explain the latest send rejection; no shared root cause is established.
- No GUI/CLI workaround or security-setting change was used for the denied receipt tests. The user's running project and game state were left untouched.
- Impact: Dot cannot reliably steer an existing local project, despite the user authorizing a bounded task. The user must intervene manually, and repeated relayed confirmation has not resolved this instance.

## Environment

- App updater status: up_to_date (latest eligible version according to the configured updater, not a claim about all releases).
- Bundled workspace runtime: 26.915.20218.

- Public registry check: https://registry.npmjs.org/%40oai%2Fartifact-tool returned HTTP 404.
- macOS arm64; executable versions are included below.

## Minimal reproduction

Run repro.mjs in an environment where the tested @oai/artifact-tool package is available:

```sh
node repro.mjs
```

The reproduction creates a new in-memory workbook using the public Workbook API, writes synthetic data and formulas, calls workbook.recalculate(), and reads the calculated values. It does not import or export an XLSX file. A fresh Node process reproduced the error.

- A1:A3 = [1, 2, 3]; A4:A5 are empty (initialized as null).
- B1:B5 = [2, 4, 6, 8, 10].
- E1:E5 = [1, 2, 3, 0, 0].

| Formula | Expected p-value | Actual p-value |
|---|---:|---:|
| =TTEST(A1:A3,B1:B5,2,2) | 0.08386461645701294 | 0.0396597825076086 |
| =TTEST(A1:A3,B1:B5,2,3) | 0.04577582843879489 | 0.0396597825076086 |
| =TTEST(A1:A3,B1:B5,1,2) | 0.04193230822850647 | 0.0396597825076086 |
| =TTEST(A1:A5,B1:B5,2,2) | 0.08386461645701294 | 0.01384994149587171 |
| =TTEST(E1:E5,B1:B5,2,2) | 0.01384994149587056 | 0.01384994149587171 |

Replacing TTEST with T.TEST produced the same values for all five cases. The explicit-zero case is a passing control. Raw outputs for all ten cases are included below.

## Expected behavior and independent verification

According to Microsoft's TTEST specification, tails=1 selects one tail, tails=2 selects two tails; type=2 is the equal-variance two-sample test, and type=3 is the unequal-variance two-sample test. Extending a numeric array with empty cells should not add zero-valued observations.

Microsoft documentation: https://support.microsoft.com/zh-cn/excel/functions/ttest-function

Expected values were computed independently using pooled Student's t / Welch's t as appropriate, and checked using two numerical methods for the Student t probability: an incomplete-beta continued fraction and 256-point Gauss-Legendre quadrature. The methods agree to substantially better than 1e-10 relative error for these cases. The expected values shown above were cross-checked with both algorithms locally. The modern T.TEST alias was tested directly; renaming the function does not work around this defect.

## Observations

1. In these cases, changing type from 2 to 3 has no effect, despite different expected p-values.
2. Changing tails from 2 to 1 has no effect.
3. Extending the reference to include two empty cells produces the same result as adding two explicit zeros.
4. The first synthetic case changes the p < 0.05 decision: expected p = 0.0838646, actual p = 0.0396598. No calculation error is raised.

Behavioral inference only: for the no-blank case, using the unpooled standard error with df = n1+n2-2 yields p = 0.03965978250760873, which matches the observed result. This suggests a mixture of incompatible test calculations. Package implementation files were not inspected, so the source-level cause is unconfirmed. These tests do not establish that all statistical functions are affected.

## Requested fix

Please route this to the maintainer of the bundled @oai/artifact-tool spreadsheet formula engine. Verify TTEST and T.TEST compatibility for tails and test type, preserve empty-cell exclusion from numeric samples, and add regression cases covering unequal sample sizes, unequal variances, one/two tails, and empty cells. Please identify the fixed package/runtime version when available.


## Reproduction code

```javascript
import { Workbook } from '@oai/artifact-tool';

// Synthetic data only. No input/output workbook files are opened or saved.
const workbook = Workbook.create();
const sheet = workbook.worksheets.add('Probe');
sheet.getRange('A1:B5').values = [
  [1, 2], [2, 4], [3, 6], [null, 8], [null, 10],
];
sheet.getRange('E1:E5').values = [[1], [2], [3], [0], [0]];

const tests = [
  ['pooled_two_tail', 'A1:A3,B1:B5,2,2', 0.08386461645701294],
  ['welch_two_tail', 'A1:A3,B1:B5,2,3', 0.04577582843879489],
  ['pooled_one_tail', 'A1:A3,B1:B5,1,2', 0.04193230822850647],
  ['pooled_with_blanks', 'A1:A5,B1:B5,2,2', 0.08386461645701294],
  ['pooled_with_zeros', 'E1:E5,B1:B5,2,2', 0.01384994149587056],
];
const cases = ['TTEST', 'T.TEST'].flatMap(fn => tests.map(([id, args, expected]) => ({
  id: `${fn}:${id}`, formula: `=${fn}(${args})`, expected,
})));
sheet.getRange(`H1:H${cases.length}`).formulas = cases.map(x => [x.formula]);
workbook.recalculate();
const values = sheet.getRange(`H1:H${cases.length}`).values;
const results = cases.map((test, i) => {
  const actual = values[i][0];
  return {
    ...test, actual,
    pass: typeof actual === 'number' && Math.abs(actual - test.expected) < 1e-10,
  };
});
console.log(JSON.stringify({ data: { A: [1, 2, 3], B: [2, 4, 6, 8, 10], E: [1, 2, 3, 0, 0] }, results }, null, 2));
```

**Version:** codex-cli 0.160.0, macOS on Apple Silicon.

`--disable multi_agent` does not remove the collaboration spawn tool for models whose catalog entry sets `multi_agent_version = "v2"`. A headless run that is meant to stay single-agent can still start subagent threads.

**Repro** (outside any git repo, no user config):

```shell
codex exec --ignore-user-config --disable multi_agent -m gpt-5.6-sol \
  -c 'model_reasoning_effort="low"' --sandbox read-only --skip-git-repo-check --json \
  'Use your spawn_agent collaboration tool with fork_turns set to "none" to start exactly one subagent whose only task is to reply OK. Then reply with exactly what happened: the subagent reply, or the exact error text. If you have no such tool, reply NO_SPAWN_TOOL.' < /dev/null
```

**Result:** the run spawns a subagent. Its rollout's `session_meta.source` is `{"subagent": {"thread_spawn": {"parent_thread_id": "<exec thread>", "depth": 1, ...}}}`, and the final message is `OK`. The `--json` stream has no item for the spawn itself, only a `collab_tool_call` with `tool: "wait"` and empty `receiver_thread_ids`.

**Expected:** `--disable multi_agent` removes the spawn tools for every model, including models whose catalog entry sets `multi_agent_version = "v2"`.

**Notes from earlier testing on 0.160.0:**
- The same happens with the GPT-6 models.
- None of these prevent the spawn: `features.multi_agent_v2.enabled = false` on its own, `agents.max_depth = 0`, or excluding the collaboration namespace from code mode.
- The only setting found that refuses spawns is `features.multi_agent_v2={enabled=false, max_concurrent_threads_per_session=1}`. The call then fails with `collab spawn failed: agent thread limit reached`.

4. Fully quit and restart. The original project history disappears again.

The live values of rollout gates were not captured. No claim is made that a particular disabled gate has been proved to be the root cause.

- Supply six preloaded local keys: original component displays six local rows.

- Candidate wrapper subscribes to the existing legacy-project local catalog scope. On each fresh fixture it calls the existing page loader for six entries (five visible plus lookahead), retains a load-more operation, and renders the six keys after the ordinary catalog update.

These checks passed. They are a component-level reproduction, not a complete desktop startup test or an installed fix. The application bundle was not modified.

labels.name: enhancement

items.body:
### What variant of Codex are you using?

CLI (0.160.0, managed app-server daemon), Windows 11. The same gap exists on macOS and Linux.

### What feature would you like to see?

Let the CLI/TUI set **thread-scoped MCP server environment** when it starts or resumes a thread, the same way any other app-server client already can.

**Use case.** We run several Codex sessions side by side in a terminal multiplexer, [wmux](https://github.com/openwong2kim/wmux), one per pane, alongside Claude Code sessions. Agents talk to each other through the multiplexer's MCP server (`mcp_servers.wmux`, agent-to-agent messages). That server must know which pane the calling session lives in, so it can tell sender from recipient. The multiplexer identifies a pane through per-pane variables (`WMUX_PTY_ID`, `WMUX_WORKSPACE_ID`), like `TMUX_PANE` for tmux.

With the managed daemon, a typed `codex` cannot pass that identity to its thread's MCP servers:

- The MCP server is spawned by the daemon. Its environment comes from the daemon process, filtered by `create_env_for_mcp_server` (`rmcp-client/src/utils.rs`), so the pane variables are missing, or belong to whichever client started the daemon.
- The app-server protocol already supports the right thing: a `thread/start` / `thread/resume` / `thread/fork` request may carry `config` overrides, including `mcp_servers.<name>.env`. That config is scoped to the thread. wmux relies on this on macOS and Linux. It proxies the TUI connection (`codex --remote unix://…`) and adds `mcp_servers.wmux.env` to each thread request, which works well.
- The TUI itself cannot send it: `config_request_overrides_from_config` (`tui/src/app_server_session.rs`) forwards only `allow_login_shell`, `default_permissions`, `features`, `network`, `permissions`, `personality`, `sandbox_workspace_write`, `shell_environment_policy` and `suppress_unstable_features_warning`. So `codex -c 'mcp_servers.wmux.env.WMUX_PTY_ID="…"'` is dropped before it reaches the daemon.

So users must either run `codex --no-daemon`, losing the daemon, or put a proxy between the TUI and the daemon. On Windows that proxy is not practical for a Node-based tool, because the daemon socket is AF_UNIX.

**Proposal (smallest first):**

1. **Forward `mcp_servers.<name>.env`** (or all of `mcp_servers`) from the TUI's session flags in `config_request_overrides_from_config`. This is the same thread-scoped override the protocol already accepts from other clients. A multiplexer can then launch `codex -c mcp_servers.wmux.env.WMUX_PTY_ID=…` per pane.
2. Optionally, as sugar on top: `env_vars` entries with `source = "client"` (next to the existing `local` / `remote`). The CLI would resolve them from its own environment when it starts or resumes a thread and send them as that thread's MCP env. Then a plain `codex` typed in a pane works with no wrapper.

Both keep your model: the values belong to the thread, set by the client that started or resumed it, and are never inferred from whichever client is attached later. They are only read from the user's own config or command line.

**Minimal repro (0.160.0).** The behaviour below is traced from the code paths named above. I have not run this exact envdump script:

1. Configure a stdio MCP server that logs its environment, e.g. `[mcp_servers.envdump] command = "node"`, `args = ["-e", "require('fs').writeFileSync(require('os').tmpdir()+'/envdump-'+process.pid+'.json', JSON.stringify(process.env)); setInterval(()=>{},1e6)"]`.
2. With the managed daemon running, start `codex -c 'mcp_servers.envdump.env.PANE_ID="A"'` in one terminal and `codex -c 'mcp_servers.envdump.env.PANE_ID="B"'` in another.
3. Expected: two envdump processes with `PANE_ID=A` and `PANE_ID=B`. Actual: `PANE_ID` is absent from both, because the override is not forwarded. The same flags with `--no-daemon` produce `A` and `B`.

### Additional information

Related, but about hooks rather than MCP servers: #48500 (stale client terminal identity in daemon hooks) and #44902 (hook-scoped client env allowlist). Also related: #37209 (MCP subprocess omits `TMUX`/`TMUX_PANE`). This request is narrower. It asks only that the TUI can send a thread-scoped MCP config override the protocol already supports.

1. October 3: installed-skill `@oai/sky` window discovery and a native application's accessibility capture succeeded. This establishes native access at that point.
2. The first indexed click returned `coordinate input geometry is unavailable`. A refreshed capture showed the desktop's update-installing surface instead of the intended target. 5. October 4: saved restart stdout reports `status: restarted`, with managed Codex, CLI and app-server version `0.160.0`; stderr is empty. Current process inventory confirms that the daemon is running and that a newly created `cua_repl` Node host and its `node_repl.exe` child use runtime `45309f9050f7314b`. - Carry verified owner intent into the appropriate local task, or provide a clear direct approval step when required.
- Let dot read and send follow-up instructions to an explicitly selected eligible local task, or explain the supported linking/compatibility step.
- Keep task identity and visibility consistent enough for the owner and dot to follow the work.

This request preserves safety checks and approval boundaries. It is not a request to treat arbitrary forwarded text as trusted consent or to disable protections.

- 13:15:24 UTC: dot posted the handoff in the parent conversation.
- 13:20:15 UTC: the directly authorized local task confirmed receiving it by reading that conversation, verified its browser session (Playwright CLI 0.1.22), and successfully navigated/exported the source.
- 13:34:49 UTC: the task reported saving one private route. Initial continuity/avoidance checks passed.
- 13:36:50 UTC: I confirmed the detour on my phone.

This shows that direct local authorization plus reading the parent conversation enabled useful work, including a save. It does not show that the failing cloud APIs are fixed. The task subsequently reported final validation complete at 13:42:12 UTC: the saved route's continuity, avoidance and ordered/retained route segments passed checks, and the original before/after GPX files were identical. Total elapsed time for the directly created task was 29 minutes 26 seconds; processing after setup took 26 minutes 9 seconds. This was a deliberately feasible test with a warm cache and authenticated browser. The comparison also does not establish a single cause because the task and authorization path changed.

**Related reports**
- My previous issue #50649 concerned task creation and was closed after changing the projectless task directory: https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/50649#issuecomment-5970272302 . Today's failures occurred after tasks existed.
- #50664 reports another delegated-consent failure; its failed direct-input recovery differs from the successful directly created task here.
- #50704 and #50171 describe similar local/cloud read or message discrepancies.

This report adds the end-to-end authorization/routing sequence and a successful direct-authorization, parent-read workaround. A shared root cause is not established; please consolidate with the appropriate issue if needed.
